run.procedureSummary: Feed: add that cycle's row to every chamber regardless of state (PUPAL too), ignoring holding limits. Overflow: process chambers 1 to 6 in order; if a chamber's mass exceeds its holding limit, the excess moves into the next chamber before that chamber is processed; excess from chamber 6 is discarded and added to the loss tally. Check: using post-overflow masses, a LARVAL chamber with mass at or above its upper mark becomes PUPAL; a PUPAL chamber with mass at or below its lower mark becomes LARVAL; otherwise no change; each change is logged with cycle and chamber. Turnover: from the post-check masses and states, compute every amount first (floor): LARVAL loses floor(m/4), which is metabolised and goes to the loss tally; PUPAL loses floor(m/2), which moves to the chamber before it (chamber i to i-1), and chamber 1's amount is discarded to the loss tally; then apply all amounts at once, ignoring limits (any excess waits for the next Overflow). Moult: if the line total after turnover is strictly over 38, every chamber becomes floor(m/2), and the removed amount (m - floor(m/2)) goes to the loss tally; states do not change. Report after cycle 5 with no further clearing of excess. All arithmetic was done with a short Python script (C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\line.py), and I checked cycle 1 by hand.

openPoints.assumption: Mass after Overflow, as the write-up's step order sets out.
States after this cycle's Check, so a chamber that changes state turns over under its new state in the same cycle.
'Over 38' means strictly greater than 38. In cycle 5 the total is exactly 38, so the moult did not fire.

openPoints.point: Moult halving rounding and amount removed
openPoints.assumption: New mass is floor(m/2), and the removed amount m - floor(m/2) (the larger half for odd masses) is discarded to the loss tally.
floor(m/4) for LARVAL and floor(m/2) for PUPAL, both computed from masses before any turnover transfer is applied.
Excess passed into chamber i+1 counts toward that chamber's own excess when its turn comes, so the excess can carry along several chambers in one pass.

openPoints.point: Excess above holding limits at end of cycle 5
openPoints.assumption: Not cleared, as the write-up says. End masses of chamber 2 (10 > 8) and chamber 4 (7 > 6) are reported as they are.
The moult changes masses only. States are next re-evaluated at the following cycle's Check.
Sum of chamber-6 overflow discards, LARVAL metabolised amounts, chamber-1 PUPAL reabsorption discards, and moult removals.
